summary: Uthmaan bin Affaan says Abu Bakr is the most worthy of the Khilaafah, being the second of the two and the Prophet's close companion.
Abu Bakr at first declines the Khilaafah, Ali and Zubayr object to being excluded from consultation, and Umar and Khaalid bin Sa'eed dispute the pledge to Abu Bakr.

people.name: Sa'd bin Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf

new_themes: unity of the Ummah after the Prophet's death
notes: Two separate reports are joined without a break (Abu Bakr's acceptance and the Khaalid bin Sa'eed episode). The speaker of the line addressed to Abu Sufyaan is unlabelled in the OCR (probably Umar). The narrator name 'Sakhar' is an OCR reading and not confirmed.

summary: Ummu Khaalid reports that her father Khaalid bin Sa'eed delayed his pledge to Abu Bakr for three months, then pledged, and later prayed for Umar.
notes: Text is garbled in places ('reported this to Bakr'); meaning taken as Umar reporting to Abu Bakr.

summary: Aa'isha reports that Abu Bakr drew his sword to ride out to Dhu Qassah alone, and Ali stopped him by recalling the Prophet's words at Uhud.
notes: Cut off mid-report: '...Abu Bakr then returned and dispatched an army instead,'.

summary: Abu Bakr tells the people he never sought the Khilaafah for ambition, returns the allegiance to them, and asks them to give it to whoever is just.
notes: Footnote references embedded in the OCR text (Kanzul Ummaal, Bidaaya) and the stray 'Saaji' debris are ignored.

summary: After the pledge, Abu Bakr tells the people to withdraw it and choose the best of them, they affirm he is best, and he counsels them on honest income and correction of leaders.
notes: Narrator printed as 'Tsa bin Atiyya' (OCR); not matched to the approved 'atiyya' entry, which is unsure.

summary: Abul Jahhaaf reports that Abu Bakr locked his door for three days after the pledge and then complained to Umar that judging was a burden, and Umar cites the Prophet's reward for a judge who errs after striving.
notes: Some words are garbled ('cancelled the pledge of complained') and the report ends mid-sentence after 'eased matters for Hadhrat Abu Bakr'.

summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr tells Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf his regrets, including not appointing Abu Ubaydah or Umar and not asking the Prophet about the succession.
new_themes: regrets at the time of death
notes: The narrator's name is repeated in the OCR text; Ansaar is a group, not a person.

summary: On his deathbed Abu Bakr consults Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf and Uthmaan about Umar, then has Uthmaan write Umar's name as successor.
notes: Narrator matched to the approved 'abu-salma-bin-abdir-rahmaan' (unsure).

summary: Uthmaan bin Ubaydullaah reports that Uthmaan bin Affaan named Umar in Abu Bakr's will, and Talha objects, to which Abu Bakr replies that he fears Allaah's questioning.

people.name: Uthmaan bin Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Umar

summary: Aa'isha reports that Abu Bakr named Umar as his successor, and when Ali and Talha question him he replies that he knows Umar best and will answer to Allaah.
Zaid bin Haarith reports that Abu Bakr wanted to appoint Umar, some people objected that Umar is harsh, and Abu Bakr replies that he fears Allaah.
notes: The objectors are unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports Umar's assassination by Abu Lu'lu'ah, Umar's consultation with Ibn Abbaas, his naming of six men to choose the next Khalifah, and his qualities for leadership.
notes: Several reports are joined (Abdullaah bin Umar, Ibn Abbaas, the 'Hasan' comment and Umar's description of a leader). 'Hasan' is marked RA in the book but is probably Hasan al-Basri (a Tabi'i), not Hasan bin Ali; not matched to the approved 'hasan' entry. Footnote debris ignored.

summary: Umar asks whether he is a Khalifah or a king, and Salmaan, Ka'b and Ibn Abil Awjaa's report affirm he is a Khalifah who takes and spends rightfully.
notes: Several reports are joined; it ends mid-verse (Surah Anfaal). Narrator Sufyaan bin Abi Awjaa is mapped to 'ibn-abil-awjaa-sulami' (likely the same person, not stated in text). 'Ka'b' is described only as a scholar of earlier scriptures, probably Ka'b al-Ahbaar; not confirmed. The Sahl bin Baydaa passage is garbled.

summary: Under the pressure of the Battle of the Confederates, the Prophet offers the Ghatafaan leaders a third of Madinah's produce and consults Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and Sa'd bin Ubaadah, who refuse.
notes: Ends mid-sentence ('They may now do their best to try to'). Uyayna bin Hisn is mapped to 'uyayna-fazaari' (same person). Footnote references to Ahmad, Tirmidhi and others are omitted.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports Haarith's demand for half of Madinah's produce, the Prophet's consultation with the Sa'ds and others who refuse, and a separate report from Musaddad on Umar.
notes: Two reports are joined; the Musaddad line is a fragment. Sa'd bin Mas'ood is not matched to any approved entry.

summary: Qaasim reports that Abu Bakr consulted a group of senior Muhaajireen and Ansaar on matters, and that they issued rulings in his time and in Umar's.
notes: Narrator 'Qaasim' is the approved 'qaasim' (unsure), not confirmed by text.

summary: Uyayna bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis ask Abu Bakr for a barren piece of land, and Umar objects that it is public property and tears up the deed.
notes: Narrator 'Ubaydah' is not in the approved list. Uyayna bin Hisn is mapped to 'uyayna-fazaari'. The final line is OCR-garbled.

summary: Aqra and Zabarqaan ask Abu Bakr for the kharaaj of Bahrain in return for a guarantee against apostasy, Umar refuses to witness and tears up the deed, and Talha is angered.
notes: Ends mid-sentence ('...disunity, the'). 'Atiyya bin Bilaal' is not matched to the approved 'atiyya'. Zabarqaan's sahabi status is not stated in the text.

summary: Umar and Uthmaan consult Ibn Abbaas on difficult matters, and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas and Umar praise his intelligence, while Umar also consulted women when needed.
notes: Several narrations are joined (Ataa, Ya'qoob, Sa'd, Ibn Shihaab). Ibn Shihaab's report is about consulting young men and women, so the Ibn Shihaab line is treated as a narrator.

summary: At Siraar Umar consults the Muhaajireen, Ansaar and army leaders, and they agree to send another companion as commander while Umar stays in Madinah to send reinforcements.
notes: The opening narrator name is garbled in the OCR ('Hadhrat Muhammad, and Ziyaad'), so both are left unmatched. The second report (Umar bin Abdul Aziz) is joined to the first. Abbaas is mapped to 'abbaas-bin-abdil-muttalib' by context only.

summary: Umar writes to Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reinforcing him with Amr bin Ma'diyakrib and Tulayha, who are to be consulted in military matters but not given command.
notes: Tulayha's sahabi status is not stated in the text.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas recounts the first expedition in Islaam under Abdullaah bin Jahash, whose men attacked a Quraysh caravan against the Prophet's wishes, and the Prophet's rebuke over disunity.
notes: The Juhayna and Banu Kinaana tribes are groups and not tagged.

summary: Shihaab Ambari reports that he set fire to the gates of Tustar when Ash'ari was struck by an arrow, and was then made Ameer over ten men of his tribe after the conquest.
notes: The text says only 'Ash'ari' and is mapped to 'abu-moosa-ashari' by context. Shihaab Ambari is not in the approved list.

summary: Umar says that when three people travel they should appoint one of them as Ameer, as the Prophet commanded.
notes: 'limar' in the OCR is Umar.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet asked each member of a large expedition to recite what Qur'aan they knew, and a young man named several surahs including Baqara.
new_themes: knowledge of the Quraan qualifies a leader
notes: Ends mid-report, before the decision on the young man is given. The young man is unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Imraan bin Abdullaah reports that Ubay bin Ka'b asked Umar why he was not given command, and Umar replied that he did not want to taint his Deen.
notes: Narrator 'Imraan bin Abdullaah' is not the approved 'imraan-bin-husayn'.

summary: Umar writes to a group of Muslims appointing Ammaar as Ameer and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood as teacher and minister, and sends Uthmaan bin Hunayf and Hudhayfa to survey Iraq's rural areas.
notes: Hudhayfa bin Yamaan may be the approved 'hudhayfa' (yes); not matched because the approved entry is bare. The recipients of the letter are not named. Wages detail (a goat a day) is not tagged.

summary: Sha'bi reports that Umar sought a man for a public post, passed over Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf, and agreed on Rabee bin Ziyaad Haarithi.
notes: OCR drops words in the middle of the question ('The people (with ...'); meaning inferred from context.

summary: Bishr bin Aasim, who failed to collect Zakaah for Umar, cites the Prophet's warning about public office, and Umar is alarmed until Abu Dharr confirms the warning.
notes: Abu Dharr's closing reply is garbled and cut ('(whom Allaah wishes to. However, ...'). Abu Waa'il's sahabi status is not stated in the text.

summary: Anas reports that the Prophet made Miqdaad an Ameer of cavalry and asked him about command after him, and Miqdaad would accept it only from Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr refused to force Abaan bin Sa'eed and sent Alaa bin Hadhrami to Bahrain.
notes: The text says 'Miqdaad bin Aswad'; mapped to 'miqdaad-bin-amr' as the same companion (Miqdad bin Amr, also called bin Aswad). Please verify. Miqdaad's exact wording in reply is partly garbled in the OCR.

summary: Umar offers Abu Hurayrah a governorship, he refuses for fear of erring in judgement, and Umar cites Yusuf as someone who sought a post.
notes: Yusuf bin Ya'qoob is the Prophet Yusuf, mapped to the approved 'yusuf' entry (no).

summary: Uthmaan asks Abdullaah bin Umar to judge between people, and Abdullaah refuses, citing a saying of the Prophet, but the report breaks off mid-quote.
notes: The Prophet's saying is cut off and garbled in the OCR.

summary: Abu Husayn reports that Mu'aawiya asked who was more worthy of the Khilaafah, and Abdullaah bin Umar began a reply about the man who struck their necks but held back for fear of losing Jannah's bounties.
notes: The text gives only 'Mu'aawiya', mapped to the bare 'muaawiya' (unsure). Context suggests Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan, but the text does not say so. The man struck is not named.

summary: Ibn Shihaab reports that when Hasan bin Ali and Mu'aawiya met, Mu'aawiya asked who was worthy of the Khilaafah, and Abdullaah bin Umar held back his reply for fear of being thought ambitious.
notes: 'tmaarn zuhri' in the OCR is read as Ibn Shihaab (Zuhri). Mu'aawiya is mapped to the bare 'muaawiya' (unsure).

summary: Several reports under one heading: Imraan bin Husayn refuses Khurasan and Hakam bin Amr is sent in his place, Abu Bakrah rebukes a man who mocked the Ameer, Ali relates the Prophet's ruling on obeying a commander who orders disobedience, and Umar and Alqama discuss obedience to the Ameer.
notes: Many separate reports are joined under one heading. 'Hasan' is probably Hasan al-Basri (marked RA in the book), not Hasan bin Ali and not the approved 'hasan'. Hudhayfa is mapped to the bare 'hudhayfa'. Zubayr bin Bakkaar is a narrator, not the approved Zubayr bin Awwaam. Two Ziyaads appear; the governor is not named.

summary: Ibn Abi Mulaykah reports that Umar told a leprous woman to stay away from Tawaaf, and after Umar died she still refused to come out, saying it was not fitting to obey him alive and disobey him dead.
notes: The woman and the passer-by are unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Shamar reports from a former governor under Ali that Ali ordered his men to obey, warning that otherwise the Jews and Christians would overpower them.
notes: The former governor is unnamed in the text.

summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates that Umar asked Abdullaah bin Umar about sitting with rulers and then speaking differently outside, and Abdullaah says the Companions regarded this as hypocrisy in the Prophet's time.
notes: Several reports are joined. The heading names Amr bin Al Aas and Abu Ubaydah, but neither appears in the text. Footnote debris ('Sayf bin Amr, also narrating from Hadhrat Hasan') is ignored. The 'Ameer' is taken to be Abu Unays, which is not confirmed.

summary: Sha'bi reports that people told Abdullaah bin Umar they flatter their rulers in person and speak differently outside, and he says the Companions regarded this as hypocrisy in the Prophet's time.
notes: The people who spoke to Abdullaah are unnamed.
